uncited: Diffusion-guided optimization methods train Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) by leveraging pretrained 2D or 3D diffusion models as priors to guide the optimization of 3D geometry and texture [S2][S4].
These methods solve the problem of 3D data scarcity and underconstrained reconstruction by distilling generative knowledge from 2D image distributions into 3D scene representations [S4].

They set themselves apart from standard NeRF training by backpropagating gradients from a frozen or jointly trained diffusion model through a differentiable renderer, rather than relying solely on photometric reconstruction losses from input images [S2].
All methods in this family optimize a NeRF representation $\theta$ (or latent codes $x$) by minimizing a loss derived from a diffusion model $\phi$.
The core mechanism involves rendering an image (or latent) from the current NeRF state, perturbing it with noise, and computing gradients based on the diffusion model's prediction of that noise.
Render an image $x$ from the NeRF at a random viewpoint.
Sample a diffusion timestep $t$ and Gaussian noise $\epsilon$.
Compute gradients $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}$ using the difference between predicted and actual noise.
The specific form of the gradient and the conditioning mechanism varies by child method.
The concept of distilling 2D diffusion priors into 3D representations was introduced by [DreamFusion](12087-dreamfusion.md) [S2][S4].

Subsequent works adapted this principle for specific domains: [DreamAvatar](12490-dreamavatar.md) for humans [S1], [Single-Stage Diffusion NeRF Training](12803-single-stage-diffusion-nerf-training.md) for joint optimization [S1], [ReconFusion](13211-reconfusion.md) for few-view reconstruction [S1], and [Nerfbusters](13427-nerfbusters.md) for artifact removal [S1].
